clue.text: One's brown animal has lost its tail in this city

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals, and the possessive 's adds S
tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: a creature that has lost its tail is missing its final letter, so the animal word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a bull is a male bovine animal

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a city, a brown creature has had its tail docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I'S, the Roman one plus a possessive S; 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to a particular city, the Turkish metropolis on the Bosphorus, once called Constantinople.

clue.text: Main milk producer?

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open ocean
a cow is the classic milk producer

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a marine mammal that suckles its young.
explanation.definitionFit: A manatee or dugong is a large plant-eating marine mammal, nicknamed for grazing like cattle and feeding its calves milk.

clue.text: Perplexed on board

explanation.definitionFit: Being lost or confused is idiomatically being out in the ocean; literally, sailors on a ship are out on the water.

clue.text: It's hard to get this fruit from south America

definitions.text: It's hard to get this fruit from south America

parts.words: It's hard to get this fruit from south America
parts.note: reads like a complaint about importing fruit, but the fruit itself is hard-shelled and named after a South American country

explanation.definitionFit: A large hard-shelled edible seed from a tall Amazonian tree, named after the biggest South American country.

clue.text: He regularly makes a bit

parts.note: sounds like someone earning a little money now and then, but the bit is the metal mouthpiece of a horse's bridle, crafted by this tradesman

explanation.surface: A man who often earns a little on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional craftsman who makes bits, spurs and other metal parts of horse harness.

clue.text: Medicine, wise man has same again

indicators.note: the first word holds the second next to it, so the pieces sit side by side in this order

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same again
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise elder repeats his prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the abbreviation of ditto, used in lists to mean 'the same again'.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured amount of a drug given at one time; loosely the medicine taken.

clue.text: Some memorandum ascribed to the writer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a note is credited to its author.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'to the writer' takes in the link word 'to'; the definition is 'the writer', which can stand in for the French novelist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was a French novelist, author of The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Audience to join in at informal gathering

definitions.text: Audience to join in at informal gathering

parts.words: Audience to join in at informal gathering
parts.note: describes an informal event where everyone present chimes in with the performer, rather than a formal audience with a dignitary

explanation.surface: A crowd is invited to take part at a casual get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal session where everyone present joins in singing familiar songs together.

clue.text: Unclear situation between black and white?

definitions.text: Unclear situation between black and white?

parts.words: Unclear situation between black and white?
parts.note: an ambiguous matter lies neither clearly one way nor the other, just as a mid tone lies between black and white

explanation.surface: Something murky that falls between two extremes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambiguous matter not clearly right or wrong, named for the shade midway between the two extremes.

clue.text: Girl, one appeared behind the wet ground

indicators.note: the single letter turns up after the other piece, so it is placed at the end

parts.note: a marsh is low-lying wet ground
one is A, as in a or one item

explanation.surface: A girl showed up at the back of the boggy field.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in the actress Marsha Hunt, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Rest did not have a hint

indicators.note: the rest word lacks the letter that follows, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: the rest is the remainder, what is left over

explanation.surface: Someone took a break without being given any clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the A from REMAINDER leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt or nudge that brings something to mind, much like a clue or hint.

clue.text: Tannery?

parts.note: a tannery treats leather hides, but here it is jokingly a place where people get a tan

explanation.definitionFit: A room or salon with sunbeds or glass walls where people bask to brown their skin.

clue.text: Has replaced fellow magician

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a different order, a fresh placing of them

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: One man has stepped in for a colleague who does conjuring.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal priest or healer believed to work magic and contact spirits.

clue.text: Check leading vehicle at airport building

parts.note: to check is to control or restrain
a tower is a vehicle that tows another, leading it along

explanation.surface: Inspect the front car on the way to the airport.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall structure at an airfield from which air traffic is directed.

clue.text: Councillor slackened having become helpless with laughter

parts.note: eased up means slackened or relaxed

explanation.surface: A local councillor relaxed and ended up in fits of giggles.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for being doubled over with mirth, as if folded by laughing.

clue.text: Item of middle gear in biblical times

definitions.text: Item of middle gear in biblical times

parts.words: Item of middle gear in biblical times
parts.note: middle gear sounds like a car's transmission, but it means clothing worn round the middle of the body, at the hips

explanation.surface: A gearbox setting from the age of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple cloth wrapped round the hips, the minimal garment of ancient times.

clue.text: Makeshift pills are dispensed

indicators.note: pills dispensed by a pharmacist are handed out, read here as their letters being shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemist hands out tablets as a temporary measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English for a last resort or stopgap, the worst option accepted.

clue.text: Reversing undertaking

parts.note: an undertaker buries a body, so reversing that work means digging it back up

explanation.definitionFit: Taking a body out of its grave, the opposite of burial by an undertaker.

clue.text: Man accommodating a supposed inhabitant from space

indicators.note: the man's name takes in, or houses, the following letter

parts.note: Martin is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man gives lodging to a visitor believed to be from another planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothetical alien from the red planet, a staple of science fiction.

clue.text: Without exception sal struggled to accept established routine

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the next piece inside them
the name struggled, so its letters writhe into a new order

parts.note: a way is a custom or established routine, as in set in one's ways

explanation.surface: Sal battled to come to terms with a set daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggled' rearranges the name, and 'to accept' puts the routine word inside it after its first two letters, so 'sal' is fodder, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Every time, on every occasion, with no case left out.

clue.text: Harass, has half of sleigh remaining

indicators.note: the opening half of the word sleigh is taken, its first three letters

explanation.surface: Someone pesters a person who has kept part of a sleigh.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or bother persistently, the same as harassing.

clue.text: Run away with girl not a writer

indicators.note: the girl's name without, or not including, the writer, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Penelope is a girl's name
a pen is something to write with, a writer

explanation.surface: A girl escapes with someone who isn't an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing PEN from PENELOPE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave secretly with a lover to marry, running off together.

clue.text: After diversion reach old town near Manchester

indicators.note: a diversion sends the letters along a different route, so they come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A traffic detour finally gets you to an old town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Greater Manchester in north-west England, birthplace of the co-operative movement.

clue.text: 500 in good health remain

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
well means in good health

explanation.surface: Five hundred people staying healthy remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay or reside somewhere, or linger, much like to remain.

clue.text: Pleased I had oil removed from flowers

parts.note: glad means pleased

indicators.note: removed is read as re-moved, moved around again, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A happy gardener had oil cleaned off the blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges OIL into OLI; 'had' and 'from' are link words, and 'Pleased' is not the definition despite opening the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a tall garden plant with sword-shaped leaves and spikes of bright blooms.

clue.text: You cannot make a comeback along this street

definitions.text: You cannot make a comeback along this street

parts.words: You cannot make a comeback along this street
parts.note: sounds like a lost cause unable to return to form, but literally traffic may not travel back in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A has-been has no chance of returning to glory here.
explanation.definitionFit: A road on which traffic may only travel in a single direction.

clue.text: Disastrously let rip a few times

indicators.note: the words go disastrously wrong, so their letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone let fly badly on several occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times as much or as many, a few times over.

clue.text: Nothing is important to this philosopher

definitions.text: Nothing is important to this philosopher

parts.words: Nothing is important to this philosopher
parts.note: reads as a remark about a carefree thinker, but literally describes one whose creed holds that values and meaning do not exist

explanation.surface: A thinker who cares about nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in a creed rejecting all moral principles and holding life meaningless; nihil is Latin for nothing.
